prime.problem: Fifteen cards of fixes, checks and speed tricks are easy to finish as fifteen separate recipes. Without the causal map that joins them, you can run train_gpt2.py but can't say which line proves the model, which one only makes it faster, and which one would silently change the result.
prime.fits: This is the front page of the last lecture, read first as the map or last as the recap. It takes the GPT from the GPT lecture and the tokenizer from the tokenizer lecture, and runs micrograd's four-step loop on them at the scale of a real 124M model.
expect: prove the module with OpenAI's weights before training it
10.82 at step 0, then overfit one batch
1000 → 90 ms per step with the same maths
val loss and HellaSwag against GPT-2's own scores
prime.goal: Draw the whole course as one causal map, from OpenAI's checkpoint to the morning-after scoreboard, and for each lever (tying, c_proj scale, precision, fusion, vocab padding, lr schedule, clip, K, eval size) say what it changes, whether it changes the result or only the speed, and the number it produced.

attend: Which cards change what the model computes, and which only change how fast the same numbers come out? Sort all fifteen.
The core formula has four additions to micrograd's update. Which card adds each one, and what goes wrong without it?
Where does the course check itself before spending compute: which three numbers can you predict before a single training step?
Why does the number 2<sup>19</sup> appear in the learning-rate schedule, the accumulation loop and the 19,073-step count at once?
Which two silent bugs in this course give plausible numbers with no error, and which check catches each?

must: Use OpenAI's names and shapes for every module → the checkpoint's 149 tensors load by name (48 of them transposed) → logits match Hugging Face to 4.58e-05 and the samples read as English → the module is proven before any training, and a random init writing word salad shows the text comes from the weights

An untrained model should spread its bets → step-0 loss ≈ ln 50,257 = 10.82 (10.96 measured) → one fixed batch must overfit (10.96 → 0.36) while fresh batches stall near the 6.3 token-frequency floor → each check isolates one part (init, backward and optimizer, data) before the expensive run

The step is memory-bound, not arithmetic-bound → fewer bits (TF32, bf16), fewer HBM round trips (torch.compile, flash attention), full tiles (vocab 50,304) and one fused update → 1000 → 90 ms on an A100, about 11×, with the loss unchanged → speed tricks never touch the update rule

GPT-3's recipe is written in tokens → divide by the 2<sup>19</sup> tokens per step → 715 warmup steps, 19,073 steps per 10B tokens, and K micro-steps each dividing its loss by K → the same mean gradient on one A100, eight, or an M3 → then judge it on shard 0 (vs 3.2924) and 10,042 HellaSwag rows (vs 29.4%)
elevated: Each Block adds to the residual stream twice → 24 adds in 12 Blocks → variances add, so the stream's std grows as √(adds) → c_proj starts at 0.02/√24 = 0.00408 → stream std 0.30 at block 12 instead of 1.54
Accuracy on n examples has noise √(p(1−p)/n) → ±0.47 points on all 10,042 HellaSwag rows, ±9.7 on 20 → 33.24 vs GPT-3's 33.7 is about one standard error, while 29.4 → 33.24 is about eight
reference: the chapter timestamps and the four section boundaries (0:13:47, 1:22:18, 2:14:55, 3:43:05)
the config: 12 layers, 12 heads, 768 wide, context 1,024, vocab 50,257 → 50,304
the recipe constants: betas (0.9, 0.95), eps 1e-8, max_lr 6e-4, min_lr 6e-5, weight decay 0.1

compress.prompt: Course-level compress: without looking, draw the whole course's causal map on one page. Start from "OpenAI released weights but not a recipe" and end at "33.24% on HellaSwag". Put the fifteen cards in four groups, draw an arrow for each because, colour the arrows that only change speed differently from the ones that change the result, and mark the two places where a missing line gives a silent wrong answer.
checklist: weights without a recipe → build the module with OpenAI's names → load, compare logits, sample: the model is proven
10.82 at step 0 → overfit one batch → a real loader → tying and the c_proj init: training from scratch is trustworthy
memory-bound step → TF32, bf16, compile, flash, 50,304, fused AdamW: 1000 → 90 ms, same loss (speed only)
GPT-3's recipe in tokens → steps via 2<sup>19</sup>; clip, warmup + cosine, decay on matrices; K micro-steps with loss / K; DDP
shard-0 val loss and HellaSwag acc_norm, against 3.2924 and 29.4%, read with their noise and their caveats
silent failures: the square c_proj loaded without .t(), and accumulation without the / K

retrieve.q: Explain to a programmer who built the GPT lecture's Shakespeare model why reproducing GPT-2 takes four more hours, when the Block itself barely changes.
answer: the architecture is the same communicate-then-compute Block, only pre-norm, with ln_f, tanh GELU and OpenAI's names
the new work is trust: a reference checkpoint to match, the 10.82 and overfit checks, and an init tuned for 24 residual adds
then cost: at 124M parameters and 10B tokens the step must be ~11× faster, which is all memory traffic
then fidelity: a borrowed recipe, a 2<sup>19</sup>-token batch built from micro-steps, and scorecards on unseen text and HellaSwag

retrieve.q: Walk through one optimizer step of the final 8×A100 run, from the loader to the updated weights, naming the card behind each line and what state changes.
answer: each of 8 ranks reads its own B = 64 × T = 1024 chunk of a uint16 shard (data-and-evals, big-batch); K = 1 here
forward under bf16 autocast, compiled, with SDPA attention, giving logits (64, 1024, 50304) and a cross-entropy loss (precision, compile-flash, first-loss)
backward fills .grad; DDP all-reduces so every rank holds the same mean gradient (big-batch)
clip_grad_norm_ to 1.0, set η from get_lr(step), fused AdamW updates θ with weight decay on matrices only (optimizer-recipe)

retrieve.q: Your lab budget allows one of: running the full HellaSwag eval (17 min), padding the vocab to 50,304, or turning on torch.compile. On the M3, which gives you information and which is mostly noise, and why?
answer: the full HellaSwag eval: it turns 3/20 (±19 points) into 2967/10042 = 0.2955 (±0.9), a number you can compare with the script's reference
vocab padding: the nice/ugly ratio wobbled 0.978 to 1.068 on MPS, so no reliable gain; it matters on CUDA kernels (96.5 → 93 ms)
torch.compile: works on MPS in torch 2.14, but one run was slower than eager (793 vs 677 ms); speedup unreliable
general lesson: measure speed tricks on your own hardware, but measure quality on a big enough eval

retrieve.q: Why do the lecture's speed changes leave the loss unchanged, while the recipe changes (warmup, clip, K) change it? Use one example from each group.
answer: speed changes compute the same function in fewer memory trips: manual, SDPA and compiled models all print loss 10.961859 on the M3
bf16 and TF32 are the exception: they round matmuls, so the loss matches only up to float noise, which Karpathy accepts
recipe changes alter the update itself: clipping rescales a norm of 48.8147 to 1.0, warmup makes step 0's lr 8.3916e-07
and dropping the / K would make the gradient K× the mean (4× in the demo: −0.306 vs −0.0765)

compare.q: The tokenizer course ended on "every vocabulary entry is a row the model must pay for and train". Where in this course do you pay for GPT-2's 50,257 entries, and which cards change that bill?
answer: wte is 50,257 × 768 = 38,597,376 numbers, 31% of the model (the target, the module)
weight tying pays for it once instead of twice: 163,037,184 → 124,439,808 (weight tying)
padding to 50,304 adds 47 rows that are never used, 36,096 params, for full tiles on the GPU (nice numbers)
the vocabulary also sets ln V = 10.82 at step 0, and 50,257 < 65,536 is why shards can be uint16 (first loss, data and evals)

compare.q: The GPT lecture trained a small GPT on 1 MB of Shakespeare and watched one loss fall. This course keeps the same Block. What is fundamentally different, which design choice causes it, and how does each one fail?
answer: same: next-token loss, communicate-then-compute Blocks on a residual stream, AdamW
different because of scale: 124M parameters and 10B tokens make cost and silent bugs the main risks, not overfitting a small text
so this course adds a reference checkpoint, a residual init scale, speed tricks, a borrowed recipe, 2<sup>19</sup>-token batches and HellaSwag
the GPT lecture fails by overfitting its 1 MB; this one fails by cost (~89 days on the M3) or by a silent bug that still trains (missing / K, untransposed c_proj)

compare.q: The big-ideas card states six claims; this overview gives one update equation. Which claims does the equation already contain, and which only show up in the levers table or the checks?
answer: in the equation: the borrowed recipe (η<sub>t</sub>, AdamW, clip) and the 2<sup>19</sup> batch built from micro-batches / K
only in the checks: writing the module with OpenAI's names, the 10.82 and overfit tests, judging on unseen text
only in the levers: the c_proj init scale and the speed ladder, which change θ's starting point or the time per step, not the rule
the equation says what each step computes; the other claims say how to trust it and how to afford it

predict.q: Your reproduction continues internet text but can't follow an instruction. The build-nanogpt README says chat finetuning "is just about swapping out the dataset and continuing the training". Before reading where-next: which parts of this course's pipeline would you keep unchanged for that, and which ones would have to change?
predict.answer: Keep the module, the loss, the core formula, AdamW with clipping, and the loop; the model and update rule don't care what the text says. Change the data (conversations instead of FineWeb-Edu), the scorecard (HellaSwag checks a base model, not whether it answers well), and probably the tokenizer's special tokens to mark who is speaking, each of which adds a row to wte and lm_head (the tokenizer course's vocab-size card). The z2h-0 where-next card points to nanochat for that pipeline, and to llm.c for the same pretraining at about 223,000 vs 185,000 tokens/s on one GPU.

apply.task: Assemble the whole training script from your own cards' pieces, not by copying train_gpt2.py: your module with tying and the c_proj init, DataLoaderLite reading two mini FineWeb-Edu shards, get_lr, clipping, accumulation with loss / K, bf16 autocast on 'mps', a val-loss check on shard 0, and your HellaSwag scorer on 20 rows. Run it at laptop size: total batch 2,048 tokens, B = 4, T = 256, 50 steps, warmup 5. Then compare its log with labs/train_gpt2.py --quick.
apply.done: Your script prints grad_accum_steps 2, a first val loss near ln 50,257 = 10.82 (the lab: 10.9518), and a val loss near 8 by step 49 (the lab: 7.9795 at its last check), with HellaSwag staying near chance (the lab: 3/20, then 4/20). The 50 steps take about 2 minutes (the lab: 104 s).
apply.hint: If the first val loss is far above 11, check the init and the tying line. If the loss falls but the printed training loss is K× too small or large, look at where you divide by K and what you add into loss_accum. At 50 × 2,048 = 102,400 tokens, beating 3.2924 is not the goal.
